defects: The environment looks like a real-time game-engine blockout: the brick is a tiled texture with no wear, grime, wet ground or bounce light, and the street geometry is plain boxes
The overall exposure is crushed: walls and street sink into murky red-black, so frames read muddy and lack a clear lighting key
The chromatic-aberration/RGB-split fringe is used as a stock effect on every sign (Isak Lindqvist, Night Chorus), not as a choice made for this piece
Whip transitions blur the frame into an unreadable smear (row 1 right, row 2 right of pairs); the motion blur hides the handoff instead of building it
The 'Mira Ovelar...' card is heavily blurred and cropped by its own glitch effect at the sampled frame, so the credit is illegible
The 'Kováč' sign is cropped and floats against black with no sense of where it sits in the street, which breaks the spatial logic
At the end the title's letters drop out ('NIGHT HO S'), so the last held frame reads like a broken render rather than a deliberate payoff
The longest shot is 4.2 s, and the end holds on a near-static title card with little camera life
The soundtrack is mostly the same regular click/hit transient repeated, over a static broadband bed; there is little tonal or melodic development
gaps: Motion: the camera language is one repeated device (a dolly past a sign, then a whip to the next). A top studio would vary the moves (rack focus, crane, a reflection or puddle reveal, signs that switch on in response to the camera) and choreograph handoffs where one sign's light or shape carries into the next, instead of hiding every transition in a blur

Finish: it needs real lighting and material work: wet asphalt reflecting the signs, volumetric haze, light spill and falloff onto the brick, weathered textures, and sign hardware like housings and cables. Without these the world reads as a placeholder, while the strongest asset (the halftone/LED letter textures in the title) sits in a dead environment

Sound: the grid of identical transients needs proper arrangement and sound design: neon hum and buzz, electrical clicks tied to each sign's ignition, street ambience, a tonal motif that builds to the title, and a resolved ending rather than a fade-out on ticks. The type styles also need a rule (each credit's sign style mapped to the role or person) so the variety means something instead of looking like a font sampler
